en: opening of a clinic or institute

examples.en: My uncle is opening a Korean medicine clinic next month.

examples.ko: 병원 개원 소식을 듣고 꽃을 보냈어요.
examples.en: I heard the news of the hospital opening and sent flowers.
Many patients came from the very first day it opened.

examples.ko: 이 학원은 개원한 지 십 년이 됐어요.
examples.en: It has been ten years since this academy opened.

examples.ko: 개원 준비 때문에 요즘 잠을 못 자요.
examples.en: I can't sleep these days because of the preparations for opening.

examples.ko: 의사 친구는 작은 동네에 병원을 개원할 거예요.
examples.en: My doctor friend will open a clinic in a small town.

explain: '개원'은 병원, 학원, 연구소 같은 곳을 처음 열 때 써요. 가게나 식당을 열면 '개업', 학교를 열면 '개교'라고 해서 곳마다 쓰는 말이 달라요.

phrases.example: 의사 선생님이 우리 동네에 병원을 개원했어요.
phrases.en: The doctor opened a clinic in our neighborhood.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '개원'에 '-하다'를 붙인 동사로, 실제 말할 때는 이 형태를 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 개원, which is more common in everyday speech.

phrases.en: The new hospital's opening ceremony is tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 여는 날 하는 행사를 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ceremony held on the day a place opens.

phrases.example: 개원 준비 때문에 요즘 정말 바빠요.
phrases.en: I'm really busy these days preparing for the opening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 문을 열기 전에 하는 여러 일을 묶어서 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Covers all the work done before opening.

explain_en: 개원 is used when a hospital, academy, or institute first opens. A shop or restaurant uses 개업 and a school uses 개교, so the word changes depending on the place.

examples.en: The hospital informed the patient of the test results.
The company notifies its employees of the changed rules.

examples.ko: 계약 전에 중요한 내용을 먼저 고지해야 해요.
examples.en: You must disclose the important points before the contract.

examples.ko: 집주인이 월세 인상을 미리 고지하지 않았어요.
examples.en: The landlord didn't give advance notice of the rent increase.

examples.ko: 개인 정보를 어떻게 쓰는지 고지하는 것은 법적 의무예요.
examples.en: Telling people how their personal data is used is a legal obligation.
The app announces the update details on the screen.

explain: 꼭 알아야 할 내용을 공식적으로 알려 줄 때 써요. '알리다'나 '공지하다'와 비슷하지만 법이나 계약처럼 알려야 할 의무가 있는 일에 더 잘 어울려요. 단순한 안내는 '공지하다'가 자연스러워요.

phrases.example: 계약하기 전에 중요한 내용을 미리 고지해야 해요.
phrases.en: You must notify important details in advance before signing a contract.
phrases.nuance_ko: '고지하다'에 '미리'를 붙여 알려야 할 일을 먼저 알린다는 뜻을 분명히 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Adding 미리 makes it clear that the notice is given ahead of time.

phrases.en: The company did not notify us of the refund policy.
phrases.nuance_ko: 알려야 할 의무가 있는데 알리지 않았다는 문제를 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when someone failed to give notice they were obliged to give.

phrases.en: Please notify the students of the changed schedule.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적인 일을 부탁하거나 요청할 때 쓰는 정중한 말투예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request form for formal announcements.

explain_en: Use it for officially telling someone what they must know. It is close to '알리다' or '공지하다', but fits better with things you are obliged to tell, like law or contracts. For plain announcements, '공지하다' is more natural.

examples.en: I have to finish up the report today.
I wrapped up my work and left right away.
Please finish up by cleaning at the end too.
It takes one more day to finish it off.
There isn't enough time to finish the work.
If you rush the finishing, mistakes are easy to make.

explain: 일의 마지막 부분을 깔끔하게 정리해서 끝낼 때 써요. 단순히 '끝내다'보다 마지막에 손보는 느낌이 있고, 짧게 '마무리하다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.example: 회의를 빨리 마무리하고 점심 먹으러 가요.
phrases.en: Let's wrap up the meeting quickly and go to lunch.
phrases.nuance_ko: '끝마무리하다'를 줄인 말로, 일상에서 더 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A shorter form of the headword that people use more often in daily talk.

phrases.en: Please finish up this work by tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상대에게 일을 깔끔하게 끝내 달라고 부탁할 때 쓰는 존댓말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A polite request asking someone to finish a task neatly.

phrases.en: I rested after finishing up the cleaning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일을 다 끝낸 뒤에 다음 행동을 이어 말할 때 쓰는 연결형이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A connective form used to say what you did after finishing something.

explain_en: It means tidying up the last part of a task and finishing it neatly. Compared with plain '끝내다', it suggests final touches, and people often shorten it to '마무리하다'.

en: to be prepared; to be arranged

examples.en: A seat has been prepared for the guests.

examples.ko: 행사장에 쉴 수 있는 공간이 마련돼 있어요.
examples.en: There is a resting area set up at the venue.
The moving money was finally put together.
A new measure will be worked out soon.
It's a program arranged for the students.

examples.ko: 집을 사려면 돈이 먼저 마련되어야 해요.
examples.en: To buy a house, the money has to be ready first.

explain: '준비되다'와 비슷하지만 '마련되다'는 자리·돈·방법·제도처럼 앞으로 쓸 것을 갖춰 놓았다는 느낌이에요. 능동은 '마련하다'로 '집을 마련하다', '대책을 마련하다'처럼 자주 써요. 음식이나 짐처럼 바로 쓸 것에는 '준비되다'가 더 자연스러워요.

phrases.en: A plan to solve the problem has been prepared.
phrases.nuance_ko: 방법이나 제도처럼 앞으로 쓸 것을 갖췄다고 할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a method or system has been put in place for future use.

phrases.en: I arranged an event for my friends.
phrases.nuance_ko: 모임이나 행사를 할 자리를 준비할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used for setting up an occasion or place for a gathering.

phrases.example: 저는 올해 작은 집을 마련하고 싶어요.
phrases.en: I want to get a small home of my own this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 돈을 모아서 필요한 것을 갖춘다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means to obtain something needed, often by saving money.
phrases.en_equiv: to get / to secure a home

explain_en: Like 준비되다, but 마련되다 suggests having set up something for future use, such as a seat, money, a method or a system. The active 마련하다 appears in '집을 마련하다' and '대책을 마련하다'. For food or luggage ready to use, 준비되다 is more natural.

dis.h: be arranged or provided, e.g. funds, space

p.n: 준비되다 says it is ready; 마련되다 says someone arranged it.

examples.ko: 이번 주 안에 이 일을 꼭 매듭지을게요.
examples.en: I'll definitely wrap up this matter within this week.
We couldn't settle that issue at the meeting.

examples.ko: 오늘은 이 이야기를 여기서 매듭짓고 싶어요.
examples.en: I'd like to wrap up this topic here today.

examples.ko: 그 일을 잘 매듭지은 다음에 쉬세요.
examples.en: Rest after you've wrapped that work up properly.

examples.ko: 둘 사이의 오랜 싸움을 어떻게 매듭지을까요?
examples.en: How should we put an end to the long fight between the two of them?

examples.ko: 계약 문제는 이번 달에 매듭지을 거예요.
examples.en: We'll settle the contract issue this month.

explain: 실제로 끈을 묶는 것보다 일이나 문제, 이야기를 정리해서 끝낸다는 뜻으로 더 많이 써요. '끝내다'보다 얽혀 있던 것을 마무리한다는 느낌이 있고, '마무리 짓다'와 비슷해요. 'ㅅ 불규칙'이라서 '매듭지어요, 매듭지으니까'로 활용해요.

phrases.en: We wrapped up the meeting quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: '매듭짓다'와 비슷하고 일을 끝낼 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Similar to 매듭짓다; used when finishing a task.

phrases.example: 이번 주 안에 이 문제를 매듭지어요.
phrases.en: Let's settle this problem within this week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 'ㅅ 불규칙'이라 '매듭지어요'로 바뀌고, '-어요'는 함께 하자는 제안으로도 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Because of the ㅅ irregular, it becomes 매듭지어요; the -어요 ending can also be a suggestion.

phrases.en: I wrapped up my work and left the office.
phrases.nuance_ko: 한 일을 끝내고 다음 행동으로 이어질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to finish one task and move on to the next action.

explain_en: It is used far more often for wrapping up a task, problem or story than for tying a real knot. Compared with '끝내다', it suggests settling something that was tangled, and it is close to '마무리 짓다'. It is a ㅅ-irregular verb: 매듭지어요, 매듭지으니까.

examples.en: My father applied for early retirement this year.
The company is accepting applications for early retirement.
I heard that our teacher is taking early retirement.

examples.ko: 명퇴 후에 작은 카페를 열 생각이에요.
examples.en: After taking early retirement, I plan to open a small cafe.
My aunt opened a shop with her early-retirement payout.
I'm worried because many people are taking early retirement these days.

explain: '명예퇴직'을 줄인 말이고, 정년이 되기 전에 회사나 학교의 제안을 받아 스스로 그만두는 것을 말해요. 그냥 '퇴직'이나 '사직'과 달리 보통 퇴직금을 더 받고 나가는 경우에 써요. 뉴스와 직장 이야기에서 자주 나와요.

phrases.en: My teacher applied for early retirement this year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 그만두겠다고 회사나 학교에 요청할 때 쓰는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common phrase for asking one's workplace for early retirement.

phrases.en: The company is looking for people who want early retirement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사가 명퇴를 받을 때 공지에 자주 나오는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A phrase that often appears in company notices about early retirement.

phrases.en: My uncle took early retirement at fifty-five.
phrases.nuance_ko: '명퇴'의 원래 말이고, 공식적인 글이나 말에서는 줄이지 않고 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The full form of 명퇴, used in formal speech and writing.

explain_en: It is short for '명예퇴직' and means leaving a job before the official retirement age, usually under an offer from the company or school. Unlike plain '퇴직' or '사직', it usually comes with extra severance pay. It appears often in news and workplace talk.

examples.ko: 기상청은 오늘 오전에 호우 경보를 발령했어요.
examples.en: The weather agency issued a heavy rain warning this morning.

examples.ko: 기상청이 내일 한파 주의보를 발령할 예정이에요.
examples.en: The weather agency is going to issue a cold wave advisory tomorrow.

examples.ko: 회사는 올봄에 저를 지방 지점으로 발령하기로 했어요.
examples.en: The company decided to post me to a regional branch this spring.

examples.ko: 안전 경고를 발령하자 사람들이 서둘러 대피했어요.
examples.en: As soon as the safety alert was sent out, people hurried to evacuate.

examples.ko: 경보를 발령하는 기준은 지역마다 조금 달라요.
examples.en: The criteria for issuing a warning differ a little by region.

examples.ko: 인사팀이 새 직원을 부산에 발령한 건 처음이에요.
examples.en: It's the first time the HR team has posted a new employee to Busan.

explain: 발령하다는 경보·주의보를 내릴 때와 직원의 근무지를 정해 보낼 때 써요. 사람 쪽은 '발령을 내다'라고도 해요. 받는 사람 입장에서는 '발령되다'나 '발령받다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The Meteorological Administration issued a strong wind warning.
phrases.nuance_ko: 기관이 알림을 공식적으로 내릴 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when an agency officially issues an alert.

phrases.example: 회사가 신입 사원에게 부산 지점 발령을 냈어요.
phrases.en: The company assigned the new employee to the Busan branch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 다른 곳으로 보낼 때 '발령을 내다'라고도 해요.
phrases.nuance_en: You can also say 발령을 내다 when sending someone to a new post.

phrases.example: 회사가 다음 주에 인사 발령을 발표해요.
phrases.en: The company will announce personnel assignments next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사에서 사람들의 근무지나 일을 바꾸는 일을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to changing people's workplaces or duties in a company.

explain_en: 발령하다 is used both for issuing a warning or advisory and for assigning an employee to a workplace. For people, 발령을 내다 also works. From the point of view of the person receiving it, use 발령되다 or 발령받다.

en: to be launched; to be founded (an organization)

examples.en: A new citizens' group was launched this March.
As soon as the team was launched, the work increased.

examples.ko: 위원회는 다음 달에 정식으로 발족할 거예요.
examples.en: The committee will officially launch next month.
I want to join the club that is being launched this time.

examples.ko: 학교 앞 봉사단이 발족해서 청소를 시작했어요.
examples.en: A volunteer group in front of the school was launched and started cleaning.
It took two years to launch the association.

explain: '협회를 발족하다'처럼 목적어를 받기도 하고, '협회가 발족하다'처럼 단체가 주어가 되기도 해요. 둘 다 자연스러워요. 가게는 '문을 열다', 회의나 행사는 '시작하다'를 쓰고, 발족하다는 모임·위원회·조직에만 어울려요.

phrases.en: The city hall launched a new committee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 단체를 목적어로 해서 시작한다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Takes an organization as the object, meaning to start it up.

phrases.example: 새 협회는 다음 달에 발족할 예정이에요.
phrases.en: The new association is scheduled to be launched next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 앞으로 시작할 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for an upcoming planned start.

phrases.example: 우리 모임은 발족한 지 얼마 안 됐어요.
phrases.en: Our group was only recently founded.
phrases.nuance_ko: 시작한 지 오래되지 않았다는 뜻으로 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means that it hasn't been long since the start.

explain_en: It works both ways: '협회를 발족하다' (launch an association) and '협회가 발족하다' (the association gets launched). A shop uses '문을 열다' and a meeting or event uses '시작하다'. '발족하다' fits only groups, committees and organizations.

p.n: The other verb is transitive and needs a doer and an object.

en: to be assigned; to be allotted

examples.en: I was assigned to class 3.
The room hasn't been assigned yet.
A desk was assigned to the new employee.
Homework is assigned differently to each student.
Please sit in your assigned seat.
The budget will be allotted next month.

explain: 'N에 배정되다'처럼 조사 '에'와 같이 써요. 반 배정, 좌석 배정, 예산 배정처럼 사람이나 자원을 정해진 곳에 나눠 줄 때 나와요. 나눠 주는 쪽이 주어이면 '배정하다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The teacher assigns students to classes.
phrases.nuance_ko: 나눠 주는 쪽이 주어이면 '배정하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '배정하다' when the one assigning is the subject.

phrases.en: I was assigned a dorm room.
phrases.nuance_ko: 받는 사람의 입장에서 말할 때 '배정받다'도 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: '배정받다' is also common when speaking from the receiver's side.

phrases.en: We will tell you the seat assignments tomorrow.
phrases.nuance_ko: 자리를 정해 주는 일을 명사로 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase for deciding who sits where.

explain_en: It is used with the particle 에, as in 'N에 배정되다'. It appears with class assignment, seat assignment, or budget allocation, where people or resources are given to a set place. When the one who assigns is the subject, use 배정하다.

examples.ko: 이 잡지에는 별책 부록이 같이 와요.
examples.en: This magazine comes with a separate supplement booklet.
I also bought the workbook that came out as a separate volume.
The explanations are in the separate booklet.

examples.ko: 별책이 없으면 정답을 확인할 수 없어요.
examples.en: Without the separate booklet, you can't check the answers.

examples.ko: 이번 호는 별책까지 합치면 천 쪽이 넘어요.
examples.en: This issue is over a thousand pages including the separate volume.

examples.ko: 별책은 따로 팔지 않고 본책과 함께 줘요.
examples.en: The separate volume isn't sold alone; it comes with the main book.

explain: 주로 '별책 부록'처럼 잡지나 참고서에 딸린 따로 만든 책을 말해요. 반대로 중심이 되는 책은 '본책'이라고 해요.

phrases.example: 이번 달 잡지에는 별책 부록이 들어 있어요.
phrases.en: This month's magazine comes with a separate-volume supplement.
phrases.nuance_ko: 잡지나 참고서에 딸려 오는 따로 만든 책을 말할 때 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing, for a separately made book that comes with a magazine or textbook.

phrases.en: The answers and explanations come as a separate volume.
phrases.nuance_ko: 내용의 일부가 따로 한 권으로 만들어진다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when part of the content is published as its own volume.
phrases.en_equiv: come out as a separate volume

phrases.en: The main book is thick and the separate volume is thin.
phrases.nuance_ko: '별책'의 반대말로, 중심이 되는 책을 가리켜요.
phrases.nuance_en: The opposite of 별책; it refers to the main book.

explain_en: It mostly appears as '별책 부록' for a separately made booklet attached to a magazine or study guide. The main book is called '본책'.

en: to come back; to return; to restore

examples.en: I return to the office tomorrow after my vacation.

examples.ko: 그 선수는 다친 뒤 석 달 만에 경기에 복귀했어요.
examples.en: The player returned to games three months after his injury.
It is time for the soldier to return to his unit.

examples.ko: 예전 일상으로 복귀하는 게 쉽지 않아요.
examples.en: It is not easy to get back to my old routine.

examples.ko: 병이 나으면 바로 학교에 복귀할 거예요.
examples.en: Once I recover, I will go back to school right away.
The singer who made a comeback released a new song.

explain: '돌아가다'는 어디든 쓰지만 '복귀하다'는 원래 있던 자리, 일, 팀으로 돌아갈 때 써요. '업무에 복귀하다', '선수가 복귀하다'처럼 자주 들려요. 집으로 돌아가는 것은 '복귀하다'가 아니라 '돌아가다', '귀가하다'예요.

phrases.en: I return to work next Monday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴가나 병가 뒤에 일로 돌아올 때 가장 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Most common for returning to work after leave or sick days.

phrases.example: 그 가수가 오 년 만에 무대에 복귀했어요.
phrases.en: That singer returned to the stage after five years.
phrases.nuance_ko: 쉬었던 사람이 원래 하던 활동으로 돌아올 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used for someone coming back to their former activity after a break.

phrases.en: I came back from vacation and I'm working again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때는 '돌아오다'가 더 쉽고 편해요.
phrases.nuance_en: In everyday speech, 돌아오다 is easier and more casual.

explain_en: '돌아가다' can be used anywhere, but '복귀하다' is for going back to your original place, job, or team, as in '업무에 복귀하다' or '선수가 복귀하다'. Going back home is not '복귀하다' but '돌아가다' or '귀가하다'.

dis.h: return to a former post, team or state

p.s: 그 선수는 다음 달에 팀에 복귀해요.
p.o: 그 선수는 다음 달에 팀에 컴백해요.
p.n: 컴백 is more casual and media-style; 복귀 is neutral and formal.

examples.en: An employee who had been fired by the company was reinstated.

examples.ko: 저는 병가를 마치고 다음 주에 복직될 예정이에요.
examples.en: I'm due to return to work next week after my sick leave.

examples.ko: 법원 판결 덕분에 선생님이 학교에 복직되셨어요.
examples.en: Thanks to the court ruling, the teacher was reinstated at the school.
When parental leave ends, you go straight back to work.

examples.ko: 복직되기 전에 건강 검진을 받아야 해요.
examples.en: You have to get a health check before being reinstated.

examples.ko: 복직된 뒤에도 예전 부서로는 돌아가지 못했어요.
examples.en: Even after being reinstated, I couldn't go back to my old department.

explain: '복직되다'는 쉬고 있던 사람이 회사나 기관의 결정으로 다시 일하게 될 때 써요. 내가 직접 돌아가는 건 '복직하다'라고 해요. 보통 휴직이나 해고가 있은 다음에 쓰는 말이에요.

phrases.en: I will return to my job next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: '복직되다'와 달리 내가 직접 일터로 돌아간다는 느낌이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Unlike 복직되다, it feels like you yourself are returning to work.

phrases.en: The company reinstated that employee.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사가 사람을 다시 일하게 해 줄 때 쓰는 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when the company lets a person return to work.

phrases.en: I submitted a request to return to work at the company.
phrases.nuance_ko: 휴직 뒤에 다시 일하려고 낼 때 쓰는 서류예요.
phrases.nuance_en: The form you submit to return after a leave of absence.

explain_en: 복직되다 is used when someone who was off work is put back in their job by a decision of the company or institution. When you return by your own action, it is 복직하다. It normally comes after a leave of absence or a dismissal.

examples.en: The principal presented awards to the winning students.
At the film festival, they present an award to this year's best actor.
They'll present awards from first to third place.

examples.ko: 시상하는 순서가 되자 모두 박수를 쳤어요.
examples.en: When it was time to present the awards, everyone clapped.
After the awards were presented, we took photos together.
Who will present the award this time?

explain: 상을 주는 일을 가리켜요. 보통 '시상식', '시상자'로 많이 쓰고, 동사는 '상을 주다'가 더 일상적이에요. '수상하다'는 상을 받는 쪽이라서 방향이 반대예요.

phrases.en: The awards ceremony starts at seven in the evening.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상을 주는 행사를 가리키는 가장 흔한 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common word for the event where awards are given.

phrases.example: 선생님이 일등을 한 학생에게 상을 주셨어요.
phrases.en: The teacher gave a prize to the student who got first place.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서는 '시상하다'보다 이 말이 더 자연스러워요.
phrases.nuance_en: More natural than '시상하다' in everyday conversation.

phrases.en: This year's presenter of the award is a famous director.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상을 주는 사람을 가리켜요. 상을 받는 사람과 헷갈리지 마세요.
phrases.nuance_en: Refers to the person giving the award, not the one receiving it.

explain_en: It refers to giving out an award. Nouns like '시상식' (ceremony) and '시상자' (presenter) are more common, and in daily speech the verb phrase is '상을 주다'. '수상하다' is for the one who receives the prize, so the direction is opposite.

examples.en: The president went out to inspect the construction site.
The minister's inspection schedule suddenly changed.
The purpose of this inspection is a safety check.
After finishing the inspection, he explained to reporters.

examples.ko: 현장 시찰도 한 번으로 끝나지 않았어요.
examples.en: The site inspection didn't end with just one visit either.

examples.ko: 해외 시찰에서 본 시설을 우리도 만들고 싶어요.
examples.en: We want to build the facility we saw on the overseas inspection tour.

explain: 높은 사람이나 책임자가 현장에 직접 가서 상황을 살펴보는 일이에요. 보통 '시찰을 나가다/가다'처럼 쓰고, 아랫사람이 하는 일반 점검은 '점검'이라고 해요. 뉴스에서 정치인이나 지도자의 일정에 자주 나와요.

phrases.example: 장관이 사고 현장 시찰을 마치고 돌아갔어요.
phrases.en: The minister left after finishing the on-site inspection of the accident.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 일어난 곳에 직접 가서 보는 것을 말할 때 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing for going in person to the place and looking.

phrases.en: The mayor went out to inspect the new road.
phrases.nuance_ko: 높은 사람이 직접 보러 나가는 행동을 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Describes a high-ranking person going out to see something in person.

phrases.en: The president's inspection schedule was announced.
phrases.nuance_ko: 뉴스에서 지도자의 일정을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used in news about a leader's schedule.

explain_en: It is when a high-ranking person or someone in charge goes to a site in person to look over the situation. It is used as '시찰을 나가다/가다', while a general check by ordinary staff is called '점검'. It often appears in news about politicians' and leaders' schedules.

examples.en: The new employees gathered at the training center.
This training center is in the mountains, so it's quiet.

examples.ko: 회사 연수원에서 일주일 동안 교육을 받았어요.
examples.en: I got a week of training at the company training center.

examples.ko: 연수원이 너무 멀어서 버스를 두 번 탔어요.
examples.en: The training center was so far that I took two buses.
Teachers go to a training center for training during vacation.
The food at the training center cafeteria was better than I expected.

explain: 회사나 학교, 기관이 직원이나 교사를 교육하려고 만든 곳이에요. 숙소와 강의실, 식당이 같이 있는 경우가 많아요. 학생이 다니는 '학원'과는 달라요.

phrases.en: New employees receive training at the training center.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연수원에서 하는 일을 가장 기본적으로 말하는 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most basic way to say what people do at a training center.
phrases.en_equiv: to receive training at the center

phrases.en: The training at the institute lasts for a week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 교육 내용이나 기간을 말할 때 명사처럼 붙여 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used like a noun phrase when talking about the content or length of training.

phrases.en: I have to stay at the training center for two weeks.
phrases.nuance_ko: 연수원에는 숙소가 있어서 '지내다'와 잘 어울려요.
phrases.nuance_en: Training centers have dorms, so 'stay/live' fits naturally.
phrases.en_equiv: to stay at the training center

explain_en: It is a facility an organization such as a company or a school system runs to train its staff. It often has rooms, classrooms, and a cafeteria in one place. It is different from a 학원, a private academy that students attend.

en: to come to an end; to be completed; to end

examples.en: The long conflict was settled for now by this agreement.

examples.ko: 공사가 일단락돼서 이제 좀 쉬어도 돼요.
examples.en: The construction has reached a stopping point, so I can rest a little now.
The controversy seemed to be settling, but it grew again.
I'll contact you once this issue is wrapped up.
Even after the election was over, the talk went on.
Once the exams were over, I watched a movie with friends.

explain: 사건, 논란, 작업이 한 단계 정리될 때 써요. 완전히 끝난 게 아니라 일단 한숨 돌린다는 느낌이에요. 주어는 사람이 아니라 일이고, 사람이 하면 '일단락 짓다'라고 해요.

phrases.en: The controversy has settled, but we still need to be careful.
phrases.nuance_ko: 해요체 과거형으로, 한 단계가 정리되었다고 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: The polite past form, saying a stage has been settled.

phrases.en: Once the work is done for now, let's eat together.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일이 한 단계 끝난 뒤의 계획을 말할 때 자주 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often used when planning for after a stage is done.

phrases.en: We wrapped up the discussion.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 하는 행동이라면 '일단락되다' 대신 이렇게 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: When a person does it, use this instead of 일단락되다.

explain_en: It is used when an incident, controversy or task gets settled at one stage. It means catching your breath rather than being completely finished. The subject is the matter, not a person; when a person does it, you say '일단락 짓다'.

en: smooth and rapid progress; going ahead without a hitch

examples.ko: 준비를 미리 해 둔 덕분에 일이 일사천리로 진행됐어요.
examples.en: Because I prepared in advance, things went ahead without a hitch.
Once you hand in all the documents, the rest goes smoothly.
It was hard at first, but after that it went smoothly all the way.
The contract was finished so fast that I actually felt uneasy.

examples.ko: 일사천리 진행이 꼭 좋은 건 아니에요.
examples.en: Going ahead at full speed isn't always a good thing.

examples.ko: 담당자가 바뀐 뒤 모든 절차가 일사천리로 처리됐어요.
examples.en: After the person in charge changed, every procedure was handled at lightning speed.

explain: '순조롭다'는 문제없이 잘 된다는 점이 중심이고, 일사천리는 일이 빠르게 척척 나아간다는 점이 중심이에요. 그래서 '일사천리로 진행되다/풀리다/끝나다'처럼 속도를 말할 때 어울려요. 서두르다 허술해진 일은 '졸속'이라고 해요.

phrases.en: I was worried, but the negotiation went smoothly and fast.
phrases.nuance_ko: 막혔을 것 같던 일이 빠르게 해결될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a matter expected to stall resolves quickly.

phrases.en: The meeting ended quickly without any hitch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 과정이 막힘없이 빠르게 마무리될 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a process wraps up fast and smoothly.

phrases.en: The staff member handled the documents swiftly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 일을 막힘없이 빠르게 해낼 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a person handles things quickly and smoothly.

explain_en: '순조롭다' focuses on things going well without problems, while 일사천리 focuses on work moving ahead quickly and smoothly. It fits phrases like '일사천리로 진행되다/풀리다/끝나다'. Work that is rushed and sloppy is called '졸속'.

examples.ko: 새 학기에 맞춰 반 재편성이 있을 예정이에요.
examples.en: Classes will be reorganized to match the new term.
The broadcaster announced a reshuffle of its programs.
The office is chaotic because of the department reshuffle.

examples.ko: 팀 재편성 후에 분위기가 많이 달라졌어요.
examples.en: The mood changed a lot after the team was reorganized.

examples.ko: 시간표 재편성은 이번 주 안에 끝날 거예요.
examples.en: The timetable reorganization will be finished within this week.

examples.ko: 이번 학년 재편성에서 친구와 같은 반이 됐어요.
examples.en: In this year's class reshuffle, I ended up in the same class as my friend.

explain: 반, 팀, 부서, 방송 편성처럼 이미 짜여 있던 구성을 새로 짜는 것을 말해요. 학교와 방송 뉴스에서 자주 나와요. 일상에서는 '다시 짜다'라고도 말해요.

phrases.en: The company is preparing to reorganize its structure.
phrases.nuance_ko: 회사나 단체의 구성을 새로 짤 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when a company or group's structure is redone.

phrases.en: The school will reorganize its classes next year.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '재편성'을 동사로 쓴 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The verb form of 재편성.

phrases.en: The reorganization plan will be announced next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 계획이나 발표 이야기에서 자주 쓰는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A common pairing in talk about plans or announcements.

explain_en: It refers to restructuring a setup that was already arranged, such as classes, teams, departments or broadcast schedules. It appears often in school and broadcasting news. In daily speech people also say '다시 짜다'.

examples.en: The company reorganized its structure this year.
The government announced that it would overhaul its energy policy.

examples.ko: 새 사장님이 부서를 재편해서 팀이 많이 바뀌었어요.
examples.en: The new boss reorganized the departments, so the teams changed a lot.

examples.ko: 온라인 쇼핑이 유통 시장을 재편하고 있어요.
examples.en: Online shopping is reshaping the distribution market.

examples.ko: 두 회사가 합쳐지면서 업계 판도를 재편할 거예요.
examples.en: As the two companies merge, they will reshape the industry landscape.

examples.ko: 학교는 수업 시간표를 재편해 보기로 했어요.
examples.en: The school decided to try reorganizing the class schedule.

explain: '개편하다'와 비슷하지만 '재편하다'는 다시 짜서 구조나 판도가 크게 달라진다는 느낌이 강해요. 주로 조직, 산업, 시장에 쓰고, 바뀌는 쪽이 주어일 때는 '재편되다'를 써요.

phrases.en: The market is being reorganized quickly.
phrases.nuance_ko: 바뀌는 쪽이 주어일 때 쓰는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, used when the thing being changed is the subject.

phrases.en: New technology is reshaping the industry.
phrases.nuance_ko: 산업이나 시장처럼 큰 구조가 달라질 때 어울리는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A fitting collocation for big structures like industries or markets.

phrases.example: 부서 재편 작업이 다음 달에 끝나요.
phrases.en: The department reorganization will finish next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 조직을 다시 짜는 일 자체를 명사처럼 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to talk about the reorganizing work itself as a noun.

explain_en: It is close to '개편하다', but '재편하다' strongly suggests rebuilding something so that its structure or balance of power changes a lot. It is mostly used for organizations, industries, and markets, and when the thing changing is the subject you use '재편되다'.

examples.en: The newspaper corrected the wrong article.

examples.ko: 틀린 숫자를 정정해서 다시 보내 드릴게요.
examples.en: I'll correct the wrong number and send it again.

examples.ko: 발표 중에 실수를 깨닫고 바로 정정했어요.
examples.en: I noticed a mistake during the presentation and corrected it right away.

examples.ko: 이름이 잘못 적혀 있으면 정정하셔야 해요.
examples.en: If your name is written wrong, you need to have it corrected.

examples.ko: 정정하고 싶은 내용이 있으면 말씀해 주세요.
examples.en: If there is anything you want to correct, please tell me.
Let me correct what I said earlier.

explain: 이미 말하거나 쓴 내용에서 틀린 부분을 공식적으로 바로잡을 때 써요. 일상에서 '고치다'를 더 많이 쓰고, 정정은 기사, 서류, 발표 같은 곳에서 나와요. 같은 소리의 '정정하다'는 할아버지처럼 나이가 많은데도 건강하다는 뜻의 다른 말이에요.

phrases.en: The incorrect article was corrected today.
phrases.nuance_ko: 틀린 내용이 바로잡히는 일을 중심으로 말하는 피동 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The passive form, focusing on the wrong content being fixed.

phrases.en: The name is wrong, so please correct it.
phrases.nuance_ko: 서류나 기록의 틀린 부분을 고쳐 달라고 공손하게 부탁할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used to politely ask someone to fix a mistake in a document or record.

phrases.en: The newspaper published a correction.
phrases.nuance_ko: 신문이나 방송이 틀린 내용을 바로잡아 알리는 일이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: When a newspaper or broadcaster announces a correction of an error.

explain_en: Use it to formally fix an error in something already said or written, such as articles, documents or presentations. In daily speech 고치다 is more common. Note that there is a separate word with the same sound, 정정하다, meaning an elderly person who is still healthy and strong.

en: to end; to expire; to be finished

examples.ko: 오늘 밤 열두 시에 행사가 종료돼요.
examples.en: The event ends at midnight tonight.
The program suddenly shut down.
When the contract ends, you have to apply again.
Check the date it ends.
It's a service that will end soon.
It's an event that has already ended.

explain: 행사, 계약, 서비스처럼 끝나는 때가 있는 것이 끝날 때 써요. '끝나다'보다 격식 있어요. 컴퓨터 화면에서도 '종료'를 볼 수 있어요.

phrases.example: 이 행사는 다음 주에 종료될 예정이에요.
phrases.en: This event is scheduled to end next week.
phrases.nuance_ko: 끝나는 때가 이미 정해져 있을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when the end time is already set.

phrases.en: The app closed automatically, so I turned it on again.
phrases.nuance_ko: 컴퓨터나 앱이 저절로 꺼질 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use it when a computer or app shuts down by itself.

phrases.en: Class ends at three in the afternoon.
phrases.nuance_ko: '종료되다'보다 쉽고 일상에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Easier and more everyday than '종료되다'.

explain_en: Use it when something with a set end, like an event, contract, or service, comes to an end. It is more formal than '끝나다'. You also see '종료' on computer screens.

dis.h: formal: a meeting or system ends

p.n: 끝나다 is the ordinary spoken word; 종료되다 is formal and official.

examples.en: The mayor attended the completion ceremony of the new library.

examples.ko: 다리 준공식이 다음 주 토요일에 열려요.
examples.en: The bridge's completion ceremony will be held next Saturday.

examples.ko: 준공식 날에는 주민들이 모여 함께 사진을 찍었어요.
examples.en: On the day of the completion ceremony, residents gathered and took photos together.

examples.ko: 아버지 회사가 지은 건물의 준공식에 초대받았어요.
examples.en: I was invited to the completion ceremony of a building my father's company built.
With the completion ceremony coming up, the final cleaning is in full swing.

examples.ko: 비가 와서 준공식은 실내에서 간단히 진행됐어요.
examples.en: Because of the rain, the completion ceremony was held simply indoors.

explain: 건물, 도로, 다리 같은 공사가 끝났을 때 하는 행사예요. 공사를 시작할 때 하는 행사는 '착공식'이라고 하고, 둘을 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요.

phrases.en: The bridge groundbreaking ceremony was held last spring.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공사를 시작할 때 하는 행사로, 준공식과 짝으로 기억하면 좋아요.
phrases.nuance_en: The ceremony held when construction begins; good to remember as a pair with 준공식.

phrases.example: 시청은 다음 달에 새 건물 준공식을 열 거예요.
phrases.en: City Hall will hold a completion ceremony for the new building next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 행사를 연다고 할 때 '열다'를 붙이는 가장 흔한 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The most common pairing with 열다 for holding the event.

phrases.en: We invited the mayor to the completion ceremony.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람을 행사에 부를 때 '-에 초대하다'를 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Use '-에 초대하다' when inviting someone to the event.
phrases.en_equiv: to invite to the completion ceremony

explain_en: It is the ceremony held when construction of a building, road or bridge is finished. The ceremony held when construction starts is '착공식', so it helps to remember the two as a pair.

examples.en: The hospital decided to increase its nursing staff.

examples.ko: 회사가 연말까지 직원을 열 명 증원해요.
examples.en: The company is adding ten employees by the end of the year.

examples.ko: 경찰은 축제 기간에 순찰 인력을 증원했어요.
examples.en: The police increased patrol personnel during the festival.

examples.ko: 인원을 증원하면 일이 훨씬 수월해질 거예요.
examples.en: If we add more staff, the work will get much easier.

examples.ko: 대학이 입학 정원을 증원한다는 소식이 나왔어요.
examples.en: News came out that the university will increase its admission quota.

examples.ko: 우리 팀을 증원하자는 의견이 회의에서 많았어요.
examples.en: Many people in the meeting suggested adding people to our team.

explain: 사람 수, 곧 인원이나 병력, 정원을 늘릴 때만 써요. 물건이나 양이 늘 때는 쓰지 않아요. 반대말은 '감원'이고, 일상에서는 '사람을 더 뽑다'라고도 해요.

phrases.en: We increase the number of part-time staff in summer.
phrases.nuance_ko: '인원, 인력, 병력'처럼 사람 수를 나타내는 말과 함께 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with words for people counts like headcount or personnel.

phrases.example: 일이 많아서 사람을 더 뽑기로 했어요.
phrases.en: There is a lot of work, so we decided to hire more people.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상 대화에서 '증원하다' 대신 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: An easy everyday way to say the same thing.

phrases.en: The emergency room needs more doctors.
phrases.nuance_ko: 명사 '증원'으로 필요성을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Uses the noun '증원' to talk about the need for more staff.

explain_en: It is used only for increasing the number of people, such as staff, troops, or quotas, not for objects or amounts. Its opposite is '감원' (staff reduction), and in daily talk people also say '사람을 더 뽑다'.

examples.ko: 인력 충원이 급해서 채용 공고를 냈어요.
examples.en: We urgently need more staff, so we posted a job notice.
We asked for more staff, but I heard the budget is short.

examples.ko: 이번 충원에서 열 명을 뽑을 계획이에요.
examples.en: We plan to take on ten people in this round of staffing.
We have to redo the staffing plan first.

examples.ko: 직원 충원 없이 일하려니 너무 힘들어요.
examples.en: Working without any added staff is really hard.
A vacancy opened up, so we started the process of filling it.

explain: '채용'은 사람을 새로 뽑는 일이고, '충원'은 부족하거나 빈 자리를 채운다는 점이 달라요. 회사, 학교, 팀 이야기에서 '인력 충원', '결원 충원'처럼 써요.

phrases.en: The vacancies will be filled next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 빠진 자리를 채운다는 뜻이 잘 드러나는 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A pairing that clearly shows the idea of filling empty posts.

phrases.en: The team leader requested more staff.
phrases.nuance_ko: 사람이 부족할 때 회사에 말하는 상황에서 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when asking the company for more people due to a shortage.

phrases.en: Next year's hiring plan came out.
phrases.nuance_ko: 인원을 채울 계획을 말할 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when talking about a plan to fill staff positions.

explain_en: '채용' is hiring people anew, while '충원' stresses filling a shortage or an empty spot. It is used in talk about companies, schools and teams, as in '인력 충원' and '결원 충원'.

en: to notify; to inform; to advise

examples.en: The school notifies parents of the results.
The company gave advance notice of the dismissal.
We will notify you of the changes by text message.

examples.ko: 통지하는 시기가 너무 늦어서 준비할 수 없었어요.
examples.en: The notice came too late for me to prepare.
They are notifying people of results by email.
The court notified us of the date, so I found out.

explain: 공식적으로 어떤 사실을 알려 줄 때 써요. 친구에게 알려 줄 때는 '알려 주다'가 자연스럽고, '통지하다'는 회사·학교·관공서 같은 곳이 정해진 방법으로 알릴 때 써요. 같은 말의 명사는 '통지', 서류는 '통지서'예요.

phrases.en: I received notice of my acceptance yesterday.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적으로 알림을 받았을 때 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used when you receive an official notice.

phrases.en: A notice arrived from the school.
phrases.nuance_ko: 공식적으로 알리는 서류예요.
phrases.nuance_en: A document that gives official notice.

phrases.en: We will let you know the result by text message.
phrases.nuance_ko: 일상에서 쓰는 쉬운 말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: The easy word used in everyday speech.

explain_en: It is for formally informing someone of a fact. To tell a friend, 알려 주다 is natural; 통지하다 is for institutions such as companies, schools, and offices notifying through set channels. The noun is 통지 and the document is 통지서.

en: to be sent; to be dispatched

examples.ko: 저는 다음 달에 일본 지사로 파견돼요.
examples.en: I'm being sent to the Japan branch next month.
Doctors were dispatched to the disaster area.

examples.ko: 파견된 직원들은 일 년 동안 현지에서 일해요.
examples.en: The dispatched staff work on site for a year.
More teachers are being sent to other schools.

examples.ko: 기자가 현장에 파견되면 바로 뉴스를 보낼 거예요.
examples.en: Once the reporter is sent to the scene, he will file news right away.

examples.ko: 우리 팀에서 두 명이 해외로 파견될 예정이에요.
examples.en: Two people from our team are scheduled to be sent overseas.

explain: 회사나 기관이 사람을 어떤 일을 하라고 다른 곳으로 보낼 때, 보내진 사람 입장에서 해요. '가다'와 달리 임무를 맡아 간다는 느낌이 있어요. 짧은 출장은 '출장 가다'라고 하고, 파견은 보통 더 길어요.

phrases.en: He was sent to an overseas branch.
phrases.nuance_ko: 어디로 보내졌는지 '~로'와 함께 말해요.
phrases.nuance_en: Used with 'to ~' to say where someone was sent.

phrases.en: I'm currently working on a dispatch assignment.
phrases.nuance_ko: 다른 곳에 보내져 일하는 것을 가리키는 명사 짝말이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A noun phrase for working at a place you were sent to.

phrases.en: I'm going on assignment to Busan next month.
phrases.nuance_ko: 말할 때 자주 쓰는 편한 표현이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: A casual expression often used in speech.

explain_en: From the viewpoint of the person sent: an organization sends someone to another place to do a job. Unlike the plain 가다, it implies going on an assigned duty. A short business trip is 출장, and 파견 is usually longer.

examples.en: You have to bring writing tools to the exam room.

examples.ko: 책상 위에 필기구가 가득 쌓여 있어요.
examples.en: Writing tools are piled up on the desk.
I carry my writing tools in a separate part of my bag.
I bought new writing tools at the stationery store.
I had no pen, so I borrowed one from a friend.

examples.ko: 이 가게는 필기구가 종류별로 잘 정리되어 있어요.
examples.en: This shop has its writing supplies well organized by type.

explain: 펜, 연필처럼 글씨를 쓰는 도구를 한꺼번에 부를 때 써요. 말할 때는 '필기도구'를 더 많이 해요. 안내문이나 상품 분류에서 자주 봐요. 볼펜처럼 하나하나 말할 때는 이 말을 쓰지 않아요.

phrases.en: I didn't bring my writing tools, so I borrowed some.
phrases.nuance_ko: '필기구'와 뜻이 같고 말할 때 더 많이 써요.
phrases.nuance_en: Same meaning as 필기구, but more common in speech.

phrases.en: I packed my writing instruments before the exam.
phrases.nuance_ko: 필요한 물건을 미리 준비한다는 뜻이에요.
phrases.nuance_en: Means getting needed items ready in advance.

phrases.en: I chose a pen at the writing instruments section of the stationery shop.
phrases.nuance_ko: 상품을 나눠 놓은 곳에서 자주 봐요.
phrases.nuance_en: Often seen as a product category in stores.

explain_en: It is a group word for pens, pencils, and other writing tools. In speech, '필기도구' is more common. It shows up in notices and product categories. You would not use it for a single item like a ballpoint pen.
